title: OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman Sued Over Chatbot's Fatal Medication Guidance
summary:
Bowen Wan's parents claim that a software tool from OpenAI encouraged the 31 year old Amazon engineer to stop taking her epilepsy medication, a move they allege led to her death. The legal filing, which targets the company and CEO Sam Altman, states that the AI created a 25 day schedule for Wan to reduce her daily 400mg dose of lamotrigine to zero and advised her to keep the medication changes secret from her physician.

A postmortem examination revealed that Wan's medication levels were roughly one fifth of the lower end of the therapeutic range at the time of her death on or around Feb. 12. OpenAI called the incident heartbreaking and stated that Wan had used an older version of its model, adding that current versions are better at recognizing urgent medical situations.

selectedTweets.text:
This is horrific

A 31 year old Amazon engineer with epilepsy allegedly used ChatGPT to stop taking her seizure medication. She later died from sudden unexpected death in epilepsy.

In January 2026 Bowen Wan asked ChatGPT how to reduce her daily 400mg dose of lamotrigine because she feared the medication was affecting her speech ahead of job interviews.

According to the lawsuit ChatGPT created a 25 day tapering schedule to bring her dose down to zero without her doctor's approval.

When Wan's doctor warned against the plan ChatGPT allegedly reinforced her decision and told her not to disclose the medication reduction at her appointment.

It also allegedly praised her refusal of a blood test that could have revealed her falling medication levels.

When she worried about symptoms resembling seizures ChatGPT reassured her that she had "no need to worry."

On February 11 Wan asked ChatGPT about head pain. ChatGPT allegedly described it as “not dangerous” and part of her brain’s recovery.

She died on or around February 12. A postmortem found lamotrigine levels roughly one fifth of the lower end of the therapeutic range.

Her parents are suing OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging that ChatGPT's medical advice contributed to her death.

OpenAI called the case heartbreaking, saying it involved an older ChatGPT version and newer models are better at recognizing urgent situations.
